questions.a: Substances that consist only of carbon and hydrogen

What is the reaction equation for the complete combustion of methane?
questions.a: Step 1 (in words): methane + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water. Step 2 (formulae): CH<sub>4</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O. Step 3 (atom balance): CH<sub>4</sub> + 2 O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub> + 2 H<sub>2</sub>O. Step 4 (simplifying): Not needed: the coefficients are already the smallest whole numbers. Reaction equation: CH<sub>4</sub>(g) + 2 O<sub>2</sub>(g) → CO<sub>2</sub>(g) + 2 H<sub>2</sub>O(l)

questions.q: What is the reaction equation for the complete combustion of propane?
questions.a: Step 1 (in words): propane + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water. Step 2 (formulae): C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O. Step 3 (atom balance): C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> + 5 O<sub>2</sub> → 3 CO<sub>2</sub> + 4 H<sub>2</sub>O. Step 4 (simplifying): Not needed: the coefficients are already the smallest whole numbers. Reaction equation: C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub>(g) + 5 O<sub>2</sub>(g) → 3 CO<sub>2</sub>(g) + 4 H<sub>2</sub>O(l)

questions.q: What is the reaction equation for the complete combustion of butane?
questions.a: Step 1 (in words): butane + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water. Step 2 (formulae): C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O. Step 3 (atom balance): C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub> + 6½ O<sub>2</sub> → 4 CO<sub>2</sub> + 5 H<sub>2</sub>O. Step 4 (simplifying): Multiply by 2: 2 C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub> + 13 O<sub>2</sub> → 8 CO<sub>2</sub> + 10 H<sub>2</sub>O. Reaction equation: 2 C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub>(g) + 13 O<sub>2</sub>(g) → 8 CO<sub>2</sub>(g) + 10 H<sub>2</sub>O(l)

questions.q: What is the reaction equation for the complete combustion of ethene?
questions.a: Step 1 (in words): ethene + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water. Step 2 (formulae): C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O. Step 3 (atom balance): C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub> + 3 O<sub>2</sub> → 2 CO<sub>2</sub> + 2 H<sub>2</sub>O. Step 4 (simplifying): Not needed: the coefficients are already the smallest whole numbers. Reaction equation: C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>(g) + 3 O<sub>2</sub>(g) → 2 CO<sub>2</sub>(g) + 2 H<sub>2</sub>O(l)

questions.q: What is the reaction equation for the complete combustion of ethanol?
questions.a: Step 1 (in words): ethanol + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water. Step 2 (formulae): C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH + O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O. Step 3 (atom balance): C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH + 3 O<sub>2</sub> → 2 CO<sub>2</sub> + 3 H<sub>2</sub>O. Step 4 (simplifying): Not needed: the coefficients are already the smallest whole numbers. Reaction equation: C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH(l) + 3 O<sub>2</sub>(g) → 2 CO<sub>2</sub>(g) + 3 H<sub>2</sub>O(l)

questions.q: Ethene reacts with bromine. What is the reaction equation?
questions.a: Step 1 (in words): ethene + bromine → 1,2-dibromoethane. Step 2 (formulae): C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub> + Br<sub>2</sub> → C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>Br<sub>2</sub>. Step 3 (atom balance): C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub> + Br<sub>2</sub> → C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>Br<sub>2</sub>. Step 4 (simplifying): Not needed: the coefficients are already the smallest whole numbers. Reaction equation: C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>(g) + Br<sub>2</sub>(l) → C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>Br<sub>2</sub>(l)

questions.q: Methane reacts with bromine under the influence of light. What is the reaction equation?
questions.a: Step 1 (in words): methane + bromine → bromomethane + hydrogen bromide. Step 2 (formulae): CH<sub>4</sub> + Br<sub>2</sub> → CH<sub>3</sub>Br + HBr. Step 3 (atom balance): CH<sub>4</sub> + Br<sub>2</sub> → CH<sub>3</sub>Br + HBr. Step 4 (simplifying): Not needed: the coefficients are already the smallest whole numbers. Reaction equation: CH<sub>4</sub>(g) + Br<sub>2</sub>(l) → CH<sub>3</sub>Br(g) + HBr(g)

questions.q: Name two uses of hydrocarbons.
questions.a: For example fuel (natural gas, petrol) and raw material for plastics

questions.q: Why is the carbon monoxide that is formed in incomplete combustion dangerous?
questions.a: It is poisonous: CO binds to the haemoglobin in the blood, so less oxygen is transported
